A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Basque instruction-tuning study. All 26 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, figures, and equations, support comparison. Relocated correlation and safety material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, model ablations, a human arena collecting 12,890 preferences from approximately 1,680 participants, and safety and bias evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports preliminary hyperparameter-search results and a manual instruction-quality analysis.

M1.justification: The Llama 3.1 backbones, Magpie instruction generation, Basque translation pipeline, training-data combinations, and 70B adaptation recipe remain unchanged. Additional validation and search documentation do not introduce a new adaptation component.

E1.justification: Training resources and Basque, English, and Spanish task coverage are retained. The stated benchmark count changes from 29 to 27 because BBQ and BasqBBQ are handled separately under safety and bias, not removed. New instruction-quality analyses examine existing training material.

E2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly reports an explicit qualitative comparison against NLLB in manual translation evaluation. v1 Section 3.3 mentions NLLB as motivation without reporting that manual comparison. Benchmark, arena, and safety comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 revises the stated repetition filter from words repeated over 100 times to repeated token sequences. v2 also reports manual sample validation and an internal arena for configuration selection. Final training settings and five-shot benchmark/four-shot bias evaluation remain unchanged; the search grid elaborates a previously mentioned search.

E4.justification: Appendix B/Table 6 adds documented sensitivity results for instruction count and training epochs, supplemented by an internal arena assessment. Appendix A.4 adds instruction-quality and translation-error analysis. The BBQ–arena correlation analysis from v1 Appendix D.1 is removed; the principal model ablations and safety analysis are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 reports p-values for nine benchmark-average/arena correlations; its replacement in v2 Figure 4 reports coefficients without p-values. Arena 90% confidence intervals and safety-annotation agreement statistics are retained.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports accuracies of 59.91/61.37 for 1M instructions at one/four epochs and 59.82/61.97 for 4M. Correlations also change: Basque average versus global arena changes from 0.84 to 0.88, and Basque ARC Challenge versus global arena from 0.75 to 0.73. Principal model accuracy, arena, and safety scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The configuration-space formulation and Bradley–Terry probability, estimation, and score transformation are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes substantive theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the stronger resource assertion that the 70B result uses no Basque data beyond the 1.2B-word corpus with the narrower assertion that it uses no Basque instructions. The main claims about corpora, bilingual instructions, instructed backbones, and scaling remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for instruction-count results and limitations concerning instruction quality and unexamined contamination. It removes the blanket safety statement of 'no observed degradation,' but strengthens the comprehension explanation from 'likely due' to 'is due.' It also removes the cross-language correlation comparability warning and the explanation of the BBQ–preference disconnect.

D1.justification: A concrete Hugging Face collection link replaces the instruction-data note 'To be released upon acceptance.' Appendix B documents the previously mentioned search settings, development-benchmark evaluation, and internal-arena selection rationale. Hardware, training-cost information, and final hyperparameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and Section 2 retains the positioning against Latxa, Llama-eus, and previous instruction-tuning research. Additional uses of existing references support expanded discussion without changing the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Selected explanations are rewritten, correlation discussion moves into Section 7, and safety material is redistributed across Sections 5.3, 7, and Appendix C.3. Most prose and the main narrative remain intact. Newly inserted instruction-language shorthand in Section 6.2 mistakenly reverses the English and Basque subscripts.

P2.justification: Appendix prose is extensively reformatted from one to two columns, with substantial float relocation. v1 Table 2 and Figure 11 are consolidated into a main-text correlation heatmap. The safety table is transposed, moved into the main text, and stripped of colored differences; a new hyperparameter-search table is added.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency by documenting the model-selection tradeoff, adding translation-error analysis, providing concrete dataset access information, and acknowledging unexamined contamination. It preserves the central evidence and removes the unsupported blanket claim of no safety degradation. Lost correlation p-values and a more categorical causal explanation temper these gains.
